title: Talking about tech
focus: download kora, charge dewa, net chole jawa, hack hoye jawa, jogajog, tothyo, goponiyota, projukti, nirapotta, protarona
body:
Kolkata talks about tech mostly in English nouns: phone, app, password, link, net. What makes it sound Bengali is the verb or phrase wrapped around the noun: charge dewa, net chole jawa, hack hoye jawa. This lesson covers those phrases, plus the real Bengali words (jogajog, tothyo, projukti) that show up in news and serious talk.

| Romanization | Bengali | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| download kora | ডাউনলোড করা | to download |
| charge dewa | চার্জ দেওয়া | to charge a phone |
| net chole jawa | নেট চলে যাওয়া | internet goes down |
| hang kora | হ্যাং করা | to freeze |
| order dewa | অর্ডার দেওয়া | to order online |
| muchhe fela | মুছে ফেলা | to delete, erase |
| hack hoye jawa | হ্যাক হয়ে যাওয়া | to get hacked |
| jogajog | যোগাযোগ | contact, communication |
| tothyo | তথ্য | information |
| goponiyota | গোপনীয়তা | privacy |
| projukti | প্রযুক্তি | technology |
| nirapotta | নিরাপত্তা | security |
| protarona | প্রতারণা | fraud, scam |

## Which word?

**English noun + Bengali verb.** Use the English noun with the Bengali verb that fits it. Some take kora (download kora, hang kora). Some take dewa (charge dewa, order dewa). Things that happen *to* you take hoye jawa (hack hoye jawa) or chole jawa (net chole jawa). Translating the noun itself (phone, app, password) makes you sound like a newsreader.

**projukti vs technology, goponiyota vs privacy.** Both are fine. In casual talk most people say the English word. In a serious conversation or when discussing the news, the Bengali word sounds educated, not bookish.

**tothyo vs khobor.** tothyo is facts and information (tothyo jogar kora = gather information). khobor is news or "what's the news" about someone.

**download kora vs namano.** download kora is neutral. namano is casual slang for songs and movies.

## Examples

- phone-ta ektu charge-e bosao, charge prai shesh: Put the phone on charge, the battery's almost dead
- net chole gechhe, meeting-e dhukte parchhi na: The internet's down, I can't get into the meeting
- app-ta update na korle kaj korbe na: The app won't work unless you update it
- bhul kore sob chhobi muchhe felechhi: I deleted all the photos by mistake
- keu OTP chaile debe na, oita protarona: Don't give an OTP to anyone who asks, that's a scam
- amar Instagram hack hoye gechhe, kichhu message korle uttor dio na: My Instagram got hacked, don't reply if I message you
- ei app-gulo tomar tothyo bikri kore: These apps sell your information
- notun projukti-r songe baba-ma tal milate pare na: My parents can't keep up with new technology
- Swiggy-te khabar order diye dao: Order the food on Swiggy
- bidesh giye-o jogajog rekho: Keep in touch even after you move abroad

cards.Example: app-ta age download kore nao: Download the app first
cards.Notes: Nobody says a Bengali word for download; the Bengali part is the verb kora. Casual slang: namano.

cards.Example: cinema-ta raate namiye rakhbo: I'll download the movie tonight
cards.Notes: Young-people slang, mostly for songs and movies (gaan namano); download kora is neutral.

cards.Example: phone-ta ektu charge dite hobe: I need to charge my phone for a bit
cards.Notes: Also charge-e bosano (put on charge). The battery itself is just 'charge': charge nei = battery's dead.

cards.Example: kotha bolte bolte charge shesh hoye gelo: The battery died in the middle of the call
cards.Notes: Kolkata says charge, not battery, for how much power is left.

cards.English: for the internet to go down
cards.Example: net chole gechhe, pore pathachhi: The internet's down, I'll send it later
cards.Notes: Same verb as current chole jawa (power cut). net = internet in speech.

cards.Example: laptop-ta bar bar hang korchhe: The laptop keeps freezing
cards.Notes: Indian English 'hang' is the standard word; also atke jawa (get stuck).

cards.Example: mash shesh, phone-e recharge korte hobe: It's the end of the month, I need to top up my phone
cards.Notes: Indian usage; nobody says top up.

cards.Example: raater khabar online-e order diye dichhi: I'm ordering dinner online
cards.Notes: Bengali uses dewa (give) with order, not kora.

cards.Example: bhul kore chhobi-gulo muchhe felechhi: I deleted the photos by mistake
cards.Notes: delete kora is just as common for files; muchhe fela also means wiping a board or erasing writing.

cards.English: to save (a number, a file) for later
cards.Example: amar number-ta save kore rakho: Save my number
cards.Notes: rakha (keep) adds 'for later'; plain save kora is also fine.

cards.Example: na jana thakle Google-e khuje dekho: If you don't know, look it up on Google
cards.Notes: search kora is equally common; khuje dekha sounds more natural in a sentence.

cards.Example: lock-ta khulte parchhi na, password bhule gechhi: I can't unlock it, I've forgotten the password
cards.Notes: password, PIN and lock stay English; khola (open) does the work.

cards.Example: amar Facebook account hack hoye gechhe: My Facebook account got hacked
cards.Notes: hoye jawa is the Bengali 'get ___ed' for things that happen to you.

cards.Example: bidesh giye-o jogajog rekho: Keep in touch even after you go abroad
cards.Notes: jogajog kora = to contact (once); jogajog rakha = to stay in contact.

cards.Example: or songe amar ar kono jogajog nei: I'm no longer in contact with him
cards.Notes: The real Bengali word, used in speech and formal writing alike; jogajog byabostha = transport/communications.

cards.Example: ei tothyo-ta tumi kotha theke pele?: Where did you get this information?
cards.Notes: khobor is news; tothyo is facts/data. Mobile 'data' stays English.

cards.Example: online-e goponiyota bole kichhu nei: There's no such thing as privacy online
cards.Notes: In casual talk people often say privacy; goponiyota is used in news and serious talk.

cards.Example: ei jontro-ta ki kaje lage?: What is this device used for?
cards.Notes: machine and gadget are also said; jontro sounds more general and is also used for 'instrument'.

cards.Example: office-er sob jontropati notun kena hoyechhe: All the office equipment was bought new
cards.Notes: Collective form of jontro; covers tools, appliances and electronics together.

cards.Example: notun projukti-r songe tal milano soja na: Keeping up with new technology isn't easy
cards.Notes: In speech 'technology' is common; projukti is standard in news and with educated speakers.

cards.Example: Salt Lake-e tothyoprojukti shilpo onek bere gechhe: The IT industry in Salt Lake has grown a lot
cards.Notes: In conversation people say IT (IT sector-e kaj kore); tothyoprojukti is the news word.

cards.Example: internet ei shotabdi-r sobcheye boro abishkar: The internet is the biggest invention of this century
cards.Notes: Also 'discovery'; abishkar kora = to invent/discover.

cards.Example: online-e taka pathanor somoy nirapotta niye sotorko theko: Be careful about security when sending money online
cards.Notes: Covers both cyber security and physical safety; nirapod = safe.

cards.Example: keu phone kore OTP chaile bujhbe protarona: If someone calls asking for an OTP, it's a scam
cards.Notes: In speech people also say fraud (as a noun or for the person: lok-ta fraud). protarok = fraudster.

cards.Example: chhele-tar phone-er nesha hoye gechhe: The boy has become addicted to his phone
cards.Notes: Also intoxication and a strong hobby (boi porar nesha = a passion for reading).

cards.Example: kritrim buddhimotta niye sobai chintito: Everyone's worried about artificial intelligence
cards.Notes: Everyday speech just says AI; this is the news and formal term.

cards.English: connection (formal, e.g. on a utility notice)
cards.Example: bill na dile bidyut songjog kete dewa hobe: If you don't pay the bill, the electricity will be cut off
cards.Notes: Spoken: connection (net-er connection kharap). songjog appears in notices and news.

cards.English: My phone is about to die.
cards.Notes: prai = almost; a very common excuse to end a call.
Kolkata says network for mobile signal; tower nei is also heard.

cards.English: Can you send me the link on WhatsApp?
cards.Notes: pathiye dewa (send over) is softer and more natural than plain pathano.
